summary: Iteration 5 (Admin + User Settings) fully validated. 37 new tests cover seeded admin login, admin guard, /api/admin/{overview,users,projects,billing,settings,ai-settings,audit-log}, suspension blocking login, cascade delete, and /api/user/{profile,password,preferences,notifications,sessions,export,account}. All 37 iter-5 + 59 iter 1-4 regression tests pass = 96/96 (100%). No backend issues found.
critical_code_review_comments: admin.py:delete_user (line 353-355) re-queries db.projects three times to build the project-id list for documents/materials/blueprints cascade. Recommend: fetch pids once into a variable, reuse — minor perf/readability fix.

admin.py:_default_preferences and _default_notifications are defined as module functions but only used inside the routers. Consider promoting them to constants or freezing the dicts to avoid accidental mutation.
admin.py:get_settings_settings doc.pop('_id', None) is called only on the freshly-inserted path; the find_one() already excludes _id via projection, so the pop is dead code (harmless).

admin.py:update_settings accepts any dict in catalog_overrides/plan_limits_overrides without validating inner keys — a misconfig (e.g. plan_limits_overrides={'free':{'max_projects':'oops'}}) would propagate to runtime quota math as a string. Add lightweight validation on tier names and value types.
admin.py:audit_log endpoint reads up to 100 rows then issues one extra users.find — fine at small scale, but for large audit logs add an index on audit_log.created_at descending.
admin.py is ~600 lines including both admin and user routers — acceptable, but if it keeps growing consider splitting into admin_router.py and user_router.py.
server.py login (line 169) checks user.get('suspended') correctly — confirmed via test_suspended_user_cannot_login. Good.

admin.py:seed_admin appends new credentials to /app/memory/test_credentials.md on every fresh seed but never trims old entries — file now contains two seeded blocks (admin@atlas.local + admin@atlas.app). Cosmetic; main agent may want to rotate or de-dupe.

user/account DELETE for admin returns 400 with a helpful message (good UX); but a non-admin's hard delete (test_non_admin_delete_then_login_401) leaves audit_log entries referencing a now-deleted actor_id — audit-log GET handles this by leaving actor_email=None, which is correct.
test_credentials: Seeded admin: admin@atlas.app / Ce#mgdP2l1E5KM*FnS02 (from /app/memory/test_credentials.md). All other tests create ephemeral test_iter5_*@example.com users with TestPass123!.
seed_data_creation: Each test creates 1-2 fresh users (no persistent seed). The settings-PUT test resets catalog_overrides/plan_limits_overrides to {} at the end so iter 1-4 free-quota regression tests still see max_projects=1.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run: pytest /app/backend/tests/ -v --tb=short. Total ~97s. Admin password is in /app/memory/test_credentials.md (latest 'admin@atlas.app' block — the earlier 'admin@atlas.local' block is from a previous boot before ADMIN_EMAIL changed). The seed_admin function is idempotent — restarting backend will not change the admin password as long as the admin user already exists. TestAdminSettings.test_put_settings_reflected mutates global system_settings but resets at the end; if this test fails partway, future regression tests for free quota may break — main agent can manually clear via mongosh: db.system_settings.updateOne({id:'global'},{$set:{plan_limits_overrides:{},catalog_overrides:{}}}).
rca of the issue: No bugs found. One self-inflicted test fixture issue during authoring: fresh_user (just registered) auto-creates a default project, so creating a second project before upgrading to Pro hit the free-plan quota gate (correct behavior). Fixed the test by first PATCHing user to pro/active via admin before creating the second project for the cascade-delete scenario.
